A.input: exact final immutable .kdna container bytes after Core admission
A.normalization: NONE; do not unpack/repack, canonicalize ZIP or remove signature
A.observation: Core computes from the single captured final byte sequence

C.entry_name_rule: Nonempty strict UTF-8 Unicode scalar path, <=4096 bytes, no control/NUL/backslash/absolute/empty/dot/dot-dot segments or trailing slash. Unique exact name bytes; no Unicode normalization. Sort by unsigned UTF-8 bytes.
C.json_entries: Every admitted name ending exactly .json is strict UTF-8 JSON, no duplicate keys at any depth, no invalid Unicode/nonfinite number; RFC8785 JCS bytes. Other admitted entries are binary exact bytes (including payload.kdnab); no guessing by content.
C.manifest_removal_rule: In kdna.json only, remove those properties if present, retain parent objects and every other property. A present /authoring must be an object under Core admission. Never recursively remove another content_digest key.
C.exclusion_rule: checksums/signature are delivery integrity evidence, not content leaves. build-receipt/reports/authoring are forbidden by runtime admission before hashing, not a route for hiding extra entries. All other admitted runtime and attachment entries are included.
C.cycle_rule: C excludes checksums/signature and the two manifest self-references; E can therefore include the final manifest containing C without a C→E→C cycle.
C.framing: ASCII KDNA-CONTENT-TREE + NUL + ASCII 0.2.0 + NUL + u32be(count); for each sorted included entry: u32be(nameByteLength) + nameUTF8 + u8(kind: JSON=0,binary=1) + u64be(contentByteLength) + canonicalJSONorExactBinary. Count/length overflow rejects; never concatenation without framing.

E.input: exact raw entry bytes for kdna.json, payload.kdnab and manifest runtime.mandatory_entries
E.set_rule: New manifest runtime.mandatory_entries is required, a duplicate-free array of valid existing entry names; required base names need not be repeated. Union with the two base entries, sort unsigned UTF-8 bytes. Missing referenced member rejects. Mandatory declarations cannot include checksums.json, signature.kdsig, mimetype or forbidden authoring entries.
E.normalization: NONE: retain raw JSON whitespace/member ordering and exact payload/attachment bytes; set membership comes from admitted manifest, never from checksums expected digest
E.framing: ASCII KDNA-RUNTIME-ENTRY-SET + NUL + ASCII 0.2.0 + NUL + u32be(count); each sorted entry: u32be(nameByteLength) + nameUTF8 + u64be(rawByteLength) + rawBytes. Same entry-name/overflow rules as C.
E.expected_rule: checksums declaration is expected comparison only; cannot supply observed E

P.input: exact complete admitted Runtime Capsule 0.2 object
P.normalization: RFC8785 JCS, strict JSON/Unicode and duplicate-key rejection before object construction
P.self_reference_rule: P is outside Capsule, never embedded and never computed by removing fields.
P.comparison: Producer computes detached P; trusted delivery evidence carries that P; Host independently recomputes P over received Capsule. All three values (producer, delivery, Host observed) must agree before matched; supplied strings do not create a Host observation.

rules: This independent authoring workflow contract applies only when a producer explicitly adopts this exact contract id, version and definition digest and separately binds its actual implementation identity, package version and exact dependency graph. A matching label alone does not establish workflow conformance. No single implementation package is the exclusive scope of this contract.

One or more real candidates may be proposed. Zero candidates reject. Selection and final confirmation are distinct actual role-bound responses; a single candidate is not automatically selected or accepted. Reject and revise remain available.

Authors explicitly distinguish a formed result from a formation rule. Missing intent never defaults to a result. Question, subject, statement, shared declarations and explicit dependencies remain distinct and are included in final preview and saved-byte verification.

Restored workspaces are untrusted editable drafts, not restored live adoption authority. New live role-correct replies and a current preview are required before formal export. Source attribution and Agent editorial decisions never imply Owner agreement.

Structural readiness is not content quality, real task success, identity verification or permission to execute actions. No requirement to invent method components, branches or unknown facts to obtain a completed-looking file.

The minimum of one genuine candidate supersedes the earlier two-candidate creation requirement only for newly authored evidence that explicitly adopts this /2 contract. The separate CS1 component interpretation definition and all Container, Payload, IR, Read and execution coordinates remain unchanged.

Contract identity and actual producer or consumer implementation identity are separate evidence. Implementations must verify both against their fixed bindings, including package identity, descriptor digest and the actual role-bound selection and independent final response. Wrong contract, changed implementation, stale confirmation or a descriptor relabel is rejected.

Historical authoring-workflow/1, creation.6, creation.7 and grammar.2 producer evidence keep their original contracts, packages and proof limits; they are never upgraded by changing a label or replayed as current /2 evidence.

resource_limits.entry_bytes_note: Raised from 5242880 on the grammar.2 coordinate so that one authored entry (the judgment payload) can carry a 100-200 issue system at realistic prose density. Author-input bounds (string_bytes, json_depth, array_length) are unchanged. total_bytes stays 12582912 and transport response_bytes stays 8388608, so 8 MiB is the aligned ceiling for both.
resource_limits.json_values_note: Maximum number of JSON values in one admitted structure. This bound was previously enforced only inside strict-input (parseJson/copyJson) and was therefore undeclared; it is declared here so the capacity ceiling is visible. The binding point is issueSnapshot's copyJson over the whole snapshot: measured 751 issues accepted and 752 rejected at 0 B of authored prose (about 133.1 values per issue).
resource_limits.string_bytes_note: This 1 MiB cap is the *author-input* bound. It is enforced by strict-input `scalarString`/`utf8` and therefore also applies wherever a serialised structure is passed through `utf8()` (for example any caller that computes `utf8(canonicalJson(x))`). The Canonical IR digest path was moved to the incremental `digestCanonical` precisely because treating the serialised IR as one string made an internally derived structure subject to an author-input limit; author input keeps the 1 MiB bound unchanged and oversize authored strings are still rejected.

admission_and_reuse.subsequent_read: Use the existing public readBrowser(snapshot, candidate, control, originalHostProvider) path against the same real snapshot; preserve all formal Read admission, Host authorization, handle, disclosure, omission, mandatory-support, budget and diagnostic precedence rules.
admission_and_reuse.request_id_consumption: After formal Read admission, at the first eligible observation entering the trusted Host gate for the bound call, atomically reserve the validated request_id before continuing that gate. Binding, lifetime and capacity remain enforced; existing policy authorization and denial handling remain unchanged. Repeated observations within that call do not consume it again. Concurrent calls cannot reserve the same ID. An already reserved ID is not made reusable by denial or delivery failure. Requests rejected by formal Read before this observation preserve their earlier diagnostics and do not reserve an ID.
admission_and_reuse.duplicate: A duplicate validated request_id fails closed by throwing a fixed internal control failure through the existing Read pipeline, which maps it to READ_TRANSPORT_FAILURE (502/null body). It is not converted into an asset denial and must not spuriously latch asset denial. This adds no Read diagnostic.
admission_and_reuse.handle_reuse: A valid issued handle may be used again with a fresh admitted request_id under the same retained provider, binding, snapshot and current authorization. Handles are not single-use tokens. Only Read owns and checks the private issuance registry; Host must not substitute a parallel authority registry.
admission_and_reuse.denial: Keep the original provider and existing Read denial latch across calls. Retention cannot lift denial, broaden scope or bypass reauthorization.
admission_and_reuse.serialization: At most one snapshot and one in-flight read exist. Excess concurrency fails closed immediately without an unbounded queue, replacing the snapshot, or corrupting the active session. An unresolved noncooperative callback retains its in-flight charge; timeout cannot falsely free capacity for another operation.

delivery.commit: Node and Express commit an eligible result only after BOTH the real server response finish event and formal Read success for that same call. A generated body, successful write invocation, returned Response or client-side observation alone is insufficient.
delivery.failure: Close, error, abort, timeout, false delivery confirmation or failed formal Read cannot commit ready content or activate pending retention. Unconfirmed delivery terminates the enabled session. A bounded control result may be delivered without representing ready content. Already transmitted physical bytes cannot be recalled; failure is not proof of zero bytes sent.
delivery.proof_limit: Server finish proves completion at that server transport boundary; it is not remote receipt, remote acknowledgement or downstream consumption.
delivery.commit_recheck: Before and after trusted delivery, recheck that the instance remains open and its trusted binding, policy epoch and deadlines are valid. Only the original prepared Read result may proceed. Read alone registers handles after its successful delivery path; Host activates pending snapshot and bytes only after the formal call returns that successful ready result.

lifecycle.ttl: An absolute monotonic lifetime starts at first preparing after trusted context verification and bounded input capture. Reads and failures do not renew it. Provider context expires_at is no later than the earlier of the absolute session deadline and independent policy expiry; existing shorter handle/context validity remains enforced. Expiry or trusted clock rollback/invalidity closes the session.
lifecycle.terminal_cleanup: On expiry, bound-context revocation, policy epoch change, unconfirmed delivery, resource termination or disposal, invalidate eligibility first, then release available Host-owned input/snapshot references, queued work, timers and listeners. Keep unresolved in-flight work charged until settlement; release the original provider after its pending calls settle. Counters accurately distinguish released resources from unsettled external work. Closed is terminal and never returns to unbound.
lifecycle.external_callbacks: A noncooperative external callback cannot be forcibly freed. Cleanup guarantees removal of owned references and prevention of late commits, not forced garbage collection of independently retained external references.
transitions: disabled: retain existing stateless behavior; valid explicit configuration starts unbound.
unbound -> preparing: first trusted binding and bounded input capture set one absolute deadline and acquire the sole in-flight slot; formal readNode performs admission.
preparing -> delivering: formal Read projection and second Host check plus complete-envelope/resource budgeting prepare one intact result.
delivering -> active: actual server finish and successful formal Read return commit the pending real snapshot and original bytes.
active -> delivering -> active: same bytes, snapshot and original provider pass fresh formal readBrowser admission, Host checks and delivery; pending work never becomes visible early.
any enabled activity -> closed: expiry, trusted clock failure, bound revocation, epoch change, disposal, unconfirmed delivery or terminal resource failure; no automatic rebind or reopen.

limits.units: Bytes are octets. MiB is 1048576 bytes. All caps are hard per retained Host session unless explicitly scoped to a call; configurations may tighten but never raise the maxima.
limits.accounting: Check capacity before retention, reservation, issuance and delivery. The retained view charge is UTF-8 byte length of plain JSON serialization of the Core inspection data view; it is an accounting charge, not JCS, a semantic digest or precise heap usage. Handle accounting includes each retained issuance record and its bounded serialized charge. Complete final responses remain subject to formal Read byte budgeting. Bounds and safe integer validation precede allocations or timer scheduling.
limits.read_counting: Every read entry consumes the bounded attempt count, including rejects and timeouts, independently of the validated request-ID set. Failures never reset or renew the count.
limits.handle_accounting: Conservatively reserve count and UTF-8 serialized metadata charge for newly prepared handles before delivery, then commit the charge after formal successful delivery. Use pending/final result metadata for resource accounting only; do not copy, mutate, delete entries from or replace the Read-owned authority registry. Final provider disposal releases that registry as a whole after pending calls settle.
limits.outer_limits: Retained calls also preserve existing multipart 12 MiB, request JSON 64 KiB and Core input limits. Read final-envelope, HTTP-frame, retained accounting and total process memory are distinct limits; none proves the others.

acceptance_obligations: Independently exercise two successful real HTTP reads with a retained issued handle, fresh request IDs, same actual Core snapshot/provider, authorized scope and mandatory support.
Exercise duplicates, invalid and foreign binding, revocation, epoch change, stale or foreign handles, expiry, disposal, concurrent reads, capacity and every byte/count/time cap.
Exercise Node and Express finish plus formal success, close/error/abort/timeout and late callbacks; prove no premature or late ready-content commit and explicit Next retained rejection.
Recheck retained-session lifecycle/limits and wire/client surfaces under the new exact Core/IR/Read binding. Generator reproducibility does not discharge runtime or consumer obligations.

host_surface.dispose: host.dispose() and server.dispose() are idempotent terminal operations. They cannot reopen a session or retract physical bytes already sent.

host_surface.error_namespace: These management/configuration failures stay Host-local. They are not ReadDiagnostic additions and cannot override an earlier formal Read error.

read_installation_guard.runtime: The existing genuine branded snapshot full VersionTuple comparison is separately mandatory; metadata-only changes cannot replace the compiled Core and Read coordinates.

rules: Only actual WHATWG Response intrinsic state is inspected; response.url must exactly match caller endpoint_url and redirected/opaque/used bodies are rejected. Context is closed caller-held data, never a network identity or Host authority.

outbound_request_json is the exact JSON string caller sent as the HTTP request field. Its strict parsed candidate supplies request_id/mode/selection/handle/budget; context correlation must match. Invalid candidates can receive admission_rejection or header-only controls, never a ready envelope.

Association IDs are consumed once per process for their bounded lifetime across all endpoint/session claims. Expired contexts reject; capacity is bounded. A new association cannot establish network replay protection or remote identity. The association must remain unexpired through body consumption and final admission; reading is bounded by the smaller of max_read_ms and remaining association lifetime.

HTTP channels are read_envelope:200 ready/422 rejected; admission_rejection:422; no_body_control:413 no JSON/body; transport_failure:502 no JSON/body. Header-only controls preserve only observed headers, never synthesize remote correlation or delivery proof.

Body reads stop at both declared and actual byte bounds or timeout; UTF-8, duplicate keys, structural limits, exact JCS bytes and generated Schema are mandatory. Content encoding other than identity is unsupported. HTTP framing is checked only as exposed by native fetch, not as raw wire framing. WebKit-normalized Transfer-Encoding: Identity is accepted with bounded decoded bytes; Simultaneously visible Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding reject, including Identity.

Ready association verifies caller tuple/asset/A/C/E, optional expected snapshot, request/receipt and handle observable bindings, mode/selection and declared full-body counts. It does not recalculate Canonical IR or authorize the remote receipt or Host.

Every result has origin=remote, explicit proof scope/limits and literal false local capabilities. It never mints or reconstructs any local opaque brand. Unverifiable remote identity/signature/PKI/revocation/network replay/third-party Host/WKWebView remain NOT_PROVEN.

carrier.definition: Explicit adoption of KDNA public static policy 2.0.0.

rules: H is SHA-256 of existing canonicalJson UTF-8 bytes with sha256: prefix. D binds this complete definition, including types and limits. The public registry is fixed and not caller configurable.

Exactly one opt-in carrier may occur at the actual owning Judgment.extensions position. It must be critical and match id, definition, contract id/version and D. Unknown critical semantics reject. Noncritical arbitrary data is never interpreted.

An opt-in requires a complete R2 rule judgment and the same owner's formation_rule. formation_rule.condition_refs must be explicitly empty; nonempty refs reject and are never erased, moved into scope, conjoined with module entries or overridden. formation_rule.policy must be absent. Every module entry expresses its complete interpreted condition within this module's scope; this exception does not relax native R2 condition or Ref rules. All R2 formalization and actual result-contract requirements remain mandatory.

rule.output_contract_ref equals both the owning result_contract.id and formation_rule.output_contract_ref. Every candidate result_type/value obeys that result contract's type, shape and cardinality. Candidates are possible declared outcomes, never already formed Result or runtime IssueResult.

Only priority strategy with explicit higher-first or lower-first direction and interpreted conditions is supported. Priority means first-matching-priority and selects at most one candidate, never all matching candidates. Traverse entries in the explicit direction. An entry whose condition is true may determine the candidate only when every earlier condition is explicitly false. If multiple conditions are true, only the earliest qualifying true entry determines the candidate. An earlier unknown or unevaluated condition blocks later candidates: it is never treated as false or skipped. Unknown strategy or condition kind rejects. Priority values are unique safe unsigned integers; array order is not priority. These are shared static interpretation rules, not execution: Core and Read do not evaluate conditions or choose a candidate.

Candidate and entry keys are unique within their respective lists. Candidate references and candidate fallback resolve locally. Duplicate keys, dangling references, wrong owner and malformed declarations reject. Fallback applies only when every entry condition is explicitly false; unknown or unevaluated conditions do not permit fallback. Fallback is either one declared candidate or explicit no_match with authored explanation; omission is not an implicit fallback. A true entry preceding an unknown later entry still determines the single candidate when all entries preceding that true entry are false. Declaring these cases does not claim that any conditions have actually been evaluated.

Names, meanings, condition statements and no_match explanations are nonempty scalar Unicode with no surrounding whitespace and exact UTF-8 limits. Canonical rule content and aggregate limits reject without truncation. Original arrays and full rule are retained; normalized candidates sort by key and entries by explicit priority direction.

rule_digest is H(authored rule). declaration_digest is H(complete decoded carrier). Core supplies the complete typed interpretation at IRNode_judgment.static_policy_interpretation, outside the authored value. It is mandatory selected-judgment body, including authored_rule, normalized rule, owner and digests. Read exact_selection and expand retain it in full and account for all required content, references, conditions and results under final-envelope budget and current Host gates; reject rather than truncate. whole_asset/catalog follow R2 deferred-body rules. No independent static_policy Ref target, Reader decoder, guessed branch relation, evaluator, action permission or runtime result is introduced.

Absence of this module does not imply an invalid simple assertion or require every judgment to have rules. Formal creation separately binds authored entries, candidates, strategy and fallback to its actual selected candidate and saved-byte evidence. Static hashes do not prove truth, identity or editorial approval.

Only critical kdna.static-policy/2 at its actual owner with this version and definition digest adopts this definition. Old /1 carriers, old definition digests, mixed identities and tampered declarations reject in the new tuple; no renaming, skipping or inferred migration is permitted. This carrier binding does not claim that migration to native R2 ConditionalPolicy has occurred.

native_binding.formation_rule_policy: must be absent; exclusive with native ConditionalPolicy
native_binding.module_scope: Candidate/entry keys and complete interpreted conditions are module-local. They do not create native R2 Ref targets or relax P.conditions/Ref/ConditionalPolicy requirements.
native_binding.projection_ownership: Core-derived typed node field, never authored Judgment input or node.value field
native_binding.selected_body: Complete interpretation is mandatory judgment body, with original authored_rule, normalized rule, actual owner and all digests retained. Exact selection and expansion apply Host gates and final complete-body budget; rejection never truncates the body.
native_binding.deferred_body: whole_asset and catalog retain R2 deferred body rules, with later lawful exact_selection and expand retrieving complete interpretation
native_binding.migration: Carrier /2 adaptation is not native ConditionalPolicy migration. Native migration requires explicit condition/Ref/priority/unknown/fallback equivalence evidence.

reference.relationship: Retains the three typed content profiles and their finite content meaning and limits. Native method/role binding is a new CS2 definition governed by S12-D002.

component.definition: Explicit adoption of KDNA public component semantics 2.0.0.

adoption.definition: Static component adoption record for KDNA public component semantics 2.0.0.

rules: H(value) is SHA-256 of existing canonicalJson UTF-8 bytes, with sha256: prefix; object keys sort by UTF-16 code units, arrays preserve original order; finite strict Unicode JSON only. D_public=H(this entire definition record). It is distinct from the frozen reference D. No caller may replace profiles, grammar, rules or D_public.

Extension.value mechanically decodes SemanticValue to ordinary JSON; duplicate record field names reject. Exact named carrier schemas and exact id/location/critical/definition are mandatory. Registered ids at any wrong position or with false critical reject. Unregistered noncritical extensions remain opaque; unknown critical extensions block. Never recursively interpret arbitrary content field names as extension instructions.

Every native component id is a real unique protocol identity. Item keys remain profile-local. Native component.method is an actual R2 basic method, and role must be legal and complete in each actual owning basic unit or top-level method. A repeated component shared by units must retain one consistent basic method and role. A profile never determines a method or answer kind.

For each CS2 opt-in, judgment_ref and component_ref resolve to the actual native owner. component_type/profile_id identify one of the three retained content profiles independently of component.method. Native base method/role, typed content and every binding are validated; same-type components, distinct roles and legal independent components are preserved.

All opt-in component bindings use target_ref equal to the owning judgment id and component_ref equal to that component; target is forbidden, and exact duplicate binding records reject. H(bindings) sorts complete binding objects by role then target_ref using unsigned UTF-8 comparisons. bindings_digest covers all roles, including an explicitly empty list. Non-opt-in native components use the disjoint local typed target branch specified by r2_semantics.native_binding; no native binding is filtered from a claimed profile digest.

component_declaration_digest=H({component:the complete native R2 MethodComponent,statement_origin}). CS2 statement_origin is authored; statement or content_ref is preserved verbatim. Native method, role, material references and body reference participate in the digest. Typed content remains a separate carrier body; it is not a replacement for the substantive authored role or the core answer.

content_digest=H(content), preserving raw item/edge/contrast order. declaration_digest=H(the complete decoded component carrier). profile, type, D, content, native component/statement origin and all bindings must match before a supported interpretation is returned. adoption_proposal_digest is a static claim, not evidence that external adoption occurred.

All declared content objects are exact. Keys match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$. Title/meaning/prompt/criterion strings are nonempty, not all whitespace, have no leading/trailing whitespace, preserve exact Unicode and satisfy UTF-8 byte limits. Duplicate local keys reject; duplicate titles remain distinct. Item arrays declare sets, no order, preference, probability, chronology, causal sequence, exclusivity or exhaustiveness.

Taxonomy content is items plus broader edges. Each endpoint resolves locally; self edges, duplicate directed edges and directed cycles reject. Multiple parents are allowed. A path may contain at most64 directed edges (initial node depth0);65 edges reject. Reachability supplies declared inclusion meaning without inventing extra authored edges. Normalized body has kind taxonomy, items sorted by key and original broader edges sorted narrowerKey then broaderKey.

Candidate-set content is items. Explicit items=[] is a supported authored empty collection, not missing/unknown/deferred or a claim the real world has none. Normalized body has kind candidate-set and items sorted by key.

Discriminator content is candidateSetRef plus items. The ref names an actual same-judgment opt-in candidate-set component. Each item has key/title/prompt and at least2 distinct candidateKey/criterion contrasts resolving to that target. Omitted candidates are not excluded. Total contrasts count as relation edges. No candidate conditions are conjoined across candidates, evaluated or converted to outcomes. Normalized body includes kind discriminator-set, unchanged candidateSetRef, all target key/title pairs as sorted candidateIndex, sorted items and contrasts sorted by candidateKey.

At most256 native components in a Payload; at most128 items and1024 edges per component; canonical content <=65536 bytes each and all opt-in content <=196608 bytes. Existing parser/resource limits apply first. Limits reject without truncation or omission. Index all declarations and simple profiles before resolving discriminators; declaration input order cannot change resolution.

R2 formal judgments explicitly supply method/components/bindings and all necessary role content. Legacy presence carriers cannot mark a required field or role undeclared. There is no presence/2 carrier and no automatic migration of CS1 presence claims.

Exactly one Payload CS2 component-adoption carrier exists iff at least one CS2 component opt-in exists. declaration_set_digest=H(all complete decoded component carrier values sorted by judgment_ref then component_ref in unsigned UTF-8 order). proposal_set_digest=H(sorted unique adoption_proposal_digest strings). CS2 D and contract identity must match. decision_digest is a claimed private decision digest; adoption_kind remains human_claim_unverified or delegated_agent_editorial. No static digest proves confirmation, identity or permission.

Formal creation retains two actual alternatives and real selected actor response, materials/interview/revision/final decision and complete candidate. A one-use host capability binds them before invoking Compiler. Versioned creation materialization kdna.studio-materialization/2 assigns judgment ids as judgment: plus lowercase full SHA-256 hex of canonicalJson([ruleId,"judgment",asset_id,judgmentLocalKey]); component ids as component: plus SHA-256 hex of canonicalJson([ruleId,"component",asset_id,judgmentLocalKey,componentLocalKey]), with ruleId kdna.studio-materialization/2 and existing canonicalJson UTF-8. Local keys match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$; duplicate local keys within their owner and any generated protocol-id collision reject without suffixing. Version is not an ID input but the complete candidate version remains bound by context. Core treats protocol ids as opaque and verifies actual ownership. The external expected materialization maps discriminator local references to those actual ids and includes original content/order/statement origin/all role targets/presence and every proposal/set/decision. After save, fresh public Core checks exact bytes against that external context. Re-signed compiler tampering and capability replay reject. Presence-only is compared even when expected component bindings are empty. An Agent editorial adoption is never relabeled human.

Core technical and complete R2 structural checks precede CS2 interpretation. No opt-in produces undeclared with null typed body and no guessed profile; it does not remove required authored role content. Valid explicit empty typed content preserves its original meaning. Invalid supported profile yields blocked interpretation; unknown critical semantics block all four R2 Read modes and never yield catalog-only disclosure.

IR judgment.method_interpretation preserves native declaration, explicit declaration presence and all typed component interpretations. Supported bodies, candidate indices, original content, provenance, binding roles and necessary source-use targets remain in the complete required closure. Asset discovery and expansion follow the new R2 four-mode contract, not the former whole_asset mode limitation.

Read uses the same Core projection and full final-envelope budget, real request/tuple/selection/snapshot binding, current Host scope/time/revocation and issued handles. No custom Reader interpreter, opaque fallback, partial criteria truncation or action permission. This public supply is not a claim to implement every private RS2 behavior.

native_binding.method_source: MethodComponent.method.term is a fixed R2 basic MethodKind. It agrees with every owning MethodUnit.method, or the top-level basic method when no units are declared.
native_binding.role_source: MethodComponent.role is an explicit R2 RoleName from that basic method template. Typed content never supplies a missing role or guesses a method.

rules.PROTECTION-PRESENCE: Manifest entitlement is optional. Absence adds no credential, lease, offline or revocable default. With presence, access must be licensed, payload encrypted true, encryption exactly payload.kdnab and profile/version must match password->kdna.envelope.aead/0.1.0 or account/org->kdna.envelope.external-grant/0.1.0. Apply to every bytes/source/producer path before payload disclosure. Existing protection markers preserve ordinary capability rejection; new malformed entitlement-only plaintext rejects as Core invalid.
rules.PROTECTION-DIGESTS: A/C/E retain original container/member byte domains. Authenticated plaintext enters the one existing Payload semantic path once. Both existing Manifest content_digest and authoring.content_digest must be refreshed, not removed. Final Manifest precedes E/checksums; legacy signature follows checksums; final A precedes external grant issuance. signature_content_digest is the independent frozen kdsig0.1 domain, not C.
rules.PROTECTION-AUTHORITY: Protected admission returns full IR only to a trusted Core caller already authorized to receive it. Same-instance opaque operations govern later controlled operations, not recall of copied IR. Pure inspect/project/Plan/Capsule do not gain clock/store/network I/O or online authority. All new controlled Reads/actions/transport commits need current protection plus independent Host scope/action checks. Disposed, cross-instance or serialized objects do not restore private authority.
rules.PROTECTION-DELIVERY: Final check then callback invocation discloses body to trusted Host. Awaiting callback across expiry cannot erase that disclosure. External transport commit separately obtains current operation validity and current Host scope. In one synchronous private transition before invoking the side-effect callback, consume the prepared token and record a unique attempt as outcome_unknown. The callback acknowledgement true confirms only its configured trusted transport handoff boundary, never remote receipt. False, throw or any thenable remains outcome_unknown even if bytes were sent. Reentrant or later reuse cannot invoke the callback again, create a new attempt or downgrade prior history. Confirmed history survives subsequent Host failure, expiry, revocation and provider error; a valid monotonic current-invocation post-ack sample is preserved even when authorization fails; an invalid, rollback, unavailable or uncalled post-ack clock records confirmed_at_ms null in the body-free failure, never an invented timestamp. Failure carries no prepared body, no ready/delivered result, and registers no new handle. No automatic retry or restoration of consumed authority. Delayed transport must acquire a distinct authorized prepared delivery at its actual handoff; no result claims global nondisclosure by a trusted Host outside this API.
rules.PROTECTION-RESULTS: R2-bound closed result unions separate actual Core failure and protection/delivery failures. All four Read modes reject unknown critical semantics with READ_UNSUPPORTED_CRITICAL; no catalog_only admission or delivery arm is active. Diagnostic references are bound to the complete R2 tuple and package combination by schema_binding. Historical pre-R2 schemas and the complete original definition remain separate and unchanged. JSON observations and receipts never create operation authority. request_failed may carry the actual rejected Read envelope only from request version dispatch (READ_MIXED_VERSION_TUPLE or READ_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION at stage version, original not_evaluated states, empty source coordinates, not_delivered receipt and exact budget). Tiny budgets preserve no_body_control. No bind/Host action or ProtectionReceipt occurs. Schema-valid later-stage rejection alone does not qualify. Binding observe/assertCurrent failures use closed ProtectionCurrentFailure with checked_at_ms UInt|null, sampled only in the current invocation. Each clock attempt resets the observation; valid monotonic samples survive later authorization/disposal rejection, while invalid/rollback/unavailable/uncalled samples are null. A timestamp is observation, not authority. Public failures project only status and diagnostic.
rules.PROTECTION-DECLARATIONS: offline/revocable absent remain unprovided. offline=false forbids offline grant use; offline=true requires a verified signed grace window and integration offline capability and does not create a window. revocable=true requires external grant plus trusted issuer status/refresh/revocation capability; password possession alone conflicts. revocable=false states no requested revocation feature and never disables actual issuer revoke/expiry. Capability conflicts reject, never silently ignore. Canonical password admission in this local Node module conflicts with offline=false because possession is locally usable.
rules.PROTECTION-CHECKSUMS: checksums.document/1 is a new closed document. Raw duplicate JSON keys reject; 1 MiB document cap, 2..128 entries, names <=4096 UTF8 bytes, member bytes <=8 MiB, total original container limits unchanged. Entries and covered_entries are the same strictly UTF8-sorted exact runtimeEntryNames set. Each entry bytes/digest matches original raw bytes. delivery_history.scope: Exactly one prepared token belongs to each protected Read attempt. Every post-preparation success/failure and commit result reports the same accumulated private history. delivery_history.transition: available -> consumed/outcome_unknown is one synchronous private transition after awaited authorization/scope observations and final local checks, before calling the transport side-effect callback. No external code runs inside that transition.
delivery_history.reentrancy: Private in-flight reservation is taken at commit entry before calling any external provider/clock callback; same-token concurrent or reentrant entry cannot start another observation or attempt. Recheck token/generation at every await. Before side-effect invocation, atomically consume token and install outcome_unknown. A pre-invocation failure closes this prepared token with not_invoked. delivery_history.acknowledgement: Only literal synchronous true confirms the configured trusted transport handoff. False/throw/thenable/invalid return leaves outcome_unknown. Never await or execute an untrusted then method to improve the result. Callback itself may already have sent data.

delivery_history.monotonicity: History is not_invoked until side-effect invocation; then outcome_unknown; then confirmed only on actual acknowledgement. delivery_history.disposal: Disposal closes authority and clears secrets best effort but retains the redacted per-token delivery history while its token/owning Read remains reachable, so a later failure cannot erase past attempts.
delivery_history.limits: not_invoked only means this token has not invoked this API transport callback. Fallback is either one declared candidate or explicit no_match with authored explanation; omission is not an implicit fallback. A true entry preceding an unknown later entry still determines the single candidate when all entries preceding that true entry are false. Names, meanings, condition statements and no_match explanations are nonempty scalar Unicode with no surrounding whitespace and exact UTF-8 limits. delivery_history.scope: Exactly one prepared token belongs to each protected Read attempt. Every post-preparation success/failure and commit result reports the same accumulated private history. Deferred new delivery requires a new protected Read with fresh checks and cannot replace an earlier token/history. Once commit fails or is outcome_unknown, later Host true cannot promote that Read to ready. Host-only success with not_invoked makes no external-delivery claim. Separate operations never import caller-supplied history.
delivery_history.transition: available -> consumed/outcome_unknown is one synchronous private transition after awaited authorization/scope observations and final local checks, before calling the transport side-effect callback. No external code runs inside that transition.
delivery_history.reentrancy: Private in-flight reservation is taken at commit entry before calling any external provider/clock callback; same-token concurrent or reentrant entry cannot start another observation or attempt. Recheck token/generation at every await. Before side-effect invocation, atomically consume token and install outcome_unknown. A pre-invocation failure closes this prepared token with not_invoked. No automatic retry; later calls return existing history only.
delivery_history.acknowledgement: Only literal synchronous true confirms the configured trusted transport handoff. False/throw/thenable/invalid return leaves outcome_unknown. Never await or execute an untrusted then method to improve the result. Callback itself may already have sent data.
delivery_history.times: Host at_ms <= attempted_at_ms <= confirmed_at_ms when available. attempted_at_ms is captured by the final trusted local check immediately before consumption. Record confirmed_at_ms from the next valid trusted-clock sample after literal true; if clock fails/rolls back, preserve confirmed with null and return a body-free provider failure. A committed success requires non-null confirmed_at_ms equal to committed_at_ms. No known timestamp may later become null.
delivery_history.monotonicity: History is not_invoked until side-effect invocation; then outcome_unknown; then confirmed only on actual acknowledgement. Never downgrade or discard attempt_id/times after throw, expiry, revocation, disposal, repeated call or final Read failure. Returned observations are frozen values at their return time; later observations report accumulated state. A retained earlier not_invoked observation cannot prove later nondisclosure.
delivery_history.disposal: Disposal closes authority and clears secrets best effort but retains the redacted per-token delivery history while its token/owning Read remains reachable, so a later failure cannot erase past attempts.
delivery_history.limits: not_invoked only means this token has not invoked this API transport callback. It is not proof that the trusted Host did not send its already received body through another route. confirmed means configured handoff acknowledgement, not confirmed remote receipt; outcome_unknown may include partial or full external disclosure.
delivery_history.outer_settlement: A prepared token can initiate commit only while its owning Host callback is active. Callback settlement closes unused authority. If a commit remains reserved or awaits authorization/scope when the outer callback settles, the owning Read returns body-free delivery_failed with zero new handles; later promise resolution/rejection cannot invoke a side effect. Preserve consumed history. Host-only true succeeds only when no failed or pending commit exists.
delivery_history.scope_recheck: Compare the full prepared body to the existing scopeBody result on a clone; filtering any content requires a new Read, even when scopeBody returns true. Final local checks after clock callbacks recheck disposed and generation.
